findings.passage: He took _Wolfs_ after reading a script that kept him in his underwear, telling Collider he was intimidated "for like a second," and he auditioned for _Whalefall_.
findings.problem: The editor added this sentence in answer to fan-03, but no opened source supports the order it asserts, and the record points the other way. IndieWire (S15, 2024-09-27, reopened) says 'when he first received the script for Wolfs, Abrams knew only that Clooney and Pitt were set to star' and quotes him: 'All I got was the interrogation scene.' The article itself quotes the first half of that answer in 'How he says yes'. Collider's question (S18, 2024-10-01) asked whether the underwear intimidated him 'while reading the script, especially since you knew you were going to work with these two major movie stars', which places the reading after he was cast. The Italian Reve (S07), cited in C124, describes reading the Weapons script, not Wolfs. The sentence credits him with knowingly choosing the Wolfs exposure, the overstatement fan-03 asked the editor to remove, so fan-03's test ('notes that... he signed onto Wolfs knowing little') is not met.
findings.acceptance_test: The Wolfs clause says he signed on knowing little ('All I got was the interrogation scene') and met the underwear script once he knew he would be working with Pitt and Clooney, intimidated 'for like a second', or it cites an opened source establishing the opposite order. Whalefall remains the clearly chosen case. C124's claim and inference are corrected, and S07 is removed from its source_ids unless it supports the claim.

findings.passage: As of his last interview on the subject, in September 2025, he had never had social media. At 13, he told Coup de Main, he had Facebook and kept asking himself, "What am I gonna say?"
findings.problem: The section's opening statement is contradicted by the next sentence. In the same Coup de Main answer (S02, reopened) he says 'I've never had it' and then 'I remember having Facebook when I was thirteen'. FAQ 3 repeats the contradiction in search-facing metadata: 'As of his September 2025 interview with Hunger, he had never had an account. He told Coup de Main in 2019 that on Facebook at 13...'. Hunger (S08, reopened) says only that he doesn't 'have an Instagram presence' and 'I felt like it might be a distraction, so I didn't do it'; it does not say he never had an account. 'Kept asking himself' also overstates S02's 'thinking, What am I gonna say?'
findings.acceptance_test: The body, FAQ 3 and the hook's 'had never had social media' describe his status without contradiction. For example: apart from a Facebook account at 13 he has stayed off social media, and as of his September 2025 Hunger interview he still had no Instagram presence. Alternatively, 'I've never had it' is attributed as his 2019 words with the Facebook exception. 'Kept asking himself' becomes 'thinking' or an equivalent. C08 and C134 are updated and keep their refresh triggers.

findings.passage: Asked in 2025 whether he brings personal experience to roles: "I think it's best to just connect with the story and really be in it."
findings.problem: Hunger's question (S08) was 'do you find yourself bringing personal experiences into these roles?', and the answer begins 'Honestly, it just depends. Sometimes aspects of yourself come through or feel similar, but in the end, I think it's best to just connect with the story'. Quoting only the last clause makes a hedged answer read as a plain no, in the paragraph that carries the revised 9-over-4 discriminator. The openness paragraph also omits two inward self-descriptions: from the same interview, when asked whether he is drawn to characters that mirror him, 'A big part of acting is exploring different aspects of yourself. Everything still comes from within'; and from Collider (S18), 'it's always you'. Neither locates identity in difference or lack, so the discriminator can survive them, but the article should show that.
findings.acceptance_test: The quote keeps or paraphrases 'it just depends... sometimes aspects of yourself come through'. The openness paragraph or the Four section acknowledges his 'everything still comes from within' framing and says in one clause why it is not identity-through-difference. C117 and C149 are updated.
